title: Bridge scheduler + async gradient prefetcher to decouple collectives from kernel launches
author: Aisha Menon
release_notes: Introduces a non-breaking 'bridge scheduler' layer and an async gradient prefetcher that improves cross-node overlap of NCCL collectives and GPU kernels; recommended rollout to canary followed by full cluster after 3-day perf validation.
description:
Summary: Add a lightweight 'bridge scheduler' shim plus an asynchronous gradient prefetcher that decouples NCCL collectives from immediate kernel launches to improve cross-node overlap and reduce end-to-end tail latency for multi-GPU tensor-parallel inference. Motivation: In high-throughput TP workloads we observed frequent stalls where collective completion was waiting on in-flight kernel launches or kernel contention, which reduced effective overlap and increased 99th percentile token latency. Existing approaches either block to finish collectives or aggressively serialize kernels, both of which harm throughput. This PR provides a scheduling bridge between the comm engine and the kernel launcher so collectives can be issued and progressed independently and their completion replayed against a lightweight kernel commit queue when the GPU is ready.
Implementation:
- Bridge scheduler: new runtime component (runtime/scheduler/bridge_scheduler.py + bridge_scheduler.cc) that holds per-peer lightweight descriptors for in-flight collectives, supports replayable completion callbacks, and maintains a small bounded window to preserve ordering semantics for TP layers.
- Async gradient prefetcher: preloads tensor shards (KV/gradients) into an on-device prefetch region and pins them with short-lived CUDA streams so the kernel when launched has warm memory locality and can immediately consume the KV without blocking the comm stream.
- NCCL tweaks: added adaptive stream tagging and a conservative threshold-based escalation that switches collective progress to host-assisted polling only when head-of-queue latency crosses per-peer SLOs.
- Kernel launch reorder: small heuristic that allows non-dependent microkernels to be reordered behind replayed collective-completion events to increase compute/comm overlap without breaking data dependencies.
- Safety and ordering: bridge scheduler enforces per-layer sequence numbers and a compact dependency bitmask to ensure correctness; fallbacks disable reordering for layers marked strict in model metadata. Benchmarks:
- Testbed: 8x A100 (80GB), BFloat16 TP-1 sharded model, synthetic e2e workload with token lengths sampled from production histograms.
- Results: median token latency unchanged, 95th latency down 18%, 99th latency down 28% in stable steady-state runs. Throughput improved 6% under mixed prompt distributions. Latency improvements held across sequence lengths 32-1024.
- Microbenchmarks: bridge scheduler adds <1.2% CPU overhead and memory overhead ~6MB per-GPU for descriptors. Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for scheduling invariants and ordering added (tests/unit/test_bridge_order.py).
- Deterministic replay tests for collectives (tests/integration/test_collective_replay.py).
- End-to-end perf harness runs included in CI (perf/harness/bridge_perf.yml); post-merge we ran a 72-hour canary on dedicated-beta with synthetic traffic.
- Safety nets: runtime flag ENABLE_BRIDGE_SCHEDULER and ConservativeSchedulerLimits env var to opt-out quickly. Rollout plan:
- Merge to main as behind-flag.
- Canary on dedicated-beta for 72 hours with canary workload and auto-rollback on perf regressions (Linear ENG-1215).
- If stable, enable for 25% of clusters for 48 hours, then 100% over 1 week. Backwards compatibility:
- No API changes.
- All behavior guarded by runtime flags and model metadata; default remains off for legacy clusters. Follow-ups:
- Tune host-assisted polling thresholds based on real traffic (ENG-1302).
- Explore persistent prefetch slabs to reduce allocation churn.
- Add telemetry to Console for per-layer replay counts and reorder events. Related: similar motivations to prior comm/compute overlap work but uses a replayable descriptor model to reduce kernel-level coupling. review_comments: Luca Martinez: Nice separation. A few correctness questions around the dependency bitmask: can we guarantee it's sufficient for XXX microkernel where partial reductions occur?
Aisha Menon (reply): We added an extra strict bit for partial-reduce kernels and a fallback path; see bridge_scheduler.cc:apply_mask() where we zero out reorder for strict bits.
Chen Wei: CI showed an intermittent integration failure on 'test_collective_replay.py' — looks like a race in the host-escalation path. Can you add a jittered backoff?
Aisha Menon (reply): Added randomized backoff and increased retry window; re-ran CI and the intermittent failure disappeared.
Maya Patel: Can we add console telemetry for per-layer replay rate?
Aisha Menon (reply): Added telemetry proto and a small exporter; ops can query via Console under 'Scheduler -> Bridge'
